question: In unicellular organisms, ______ is the method of reproduction.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Fission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fission** is the primary method of **asexual reproduction** in **unicellular organisms** such as **bacteria**, **archaea**, and many **protozoa**.
 
• In this process, a single parent cell divides into two or more independent daughter cells. It involves the division of the **nucleus** (**karyokinesis**) followed by the division of the **cytoplasm** (**cytokinesis**).
 
• **Binary Fission**: This is the most common form where the parent organism splits into **two** equal halves. For example, **Amoeba** undergoes binary fission in any plane, while **Leishmania** (which causes kala-azar) undergoes fission in a specific orientation relative to its whip-like structures.
 
• **Multiple Fission**: In this type, the parent cell divides into **many** daughter cells simultaneously. This is often observed in the malarial parasite, **Plasmodium**, especially during unfavorable conditions.
 
• Since there is no fusion of **gametes**, the offspring produced are genetically identical to the parent, often referred to as **clones**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fragmentation**:
 
 
• This is a method of reproduction found in **multicellular organisms** with relatively simple body designs.
 
• An organism simply breaks up into smaller pieces upon maturation, and each piece grows into a new individual.
 
• A classic example is **Spirogyra**, a filamentous **alga**.
 
 
 
• **Regeneration**:
 
 
• If an individual is somehow cut or broken into many pieces, many of these pieces grow into separate individuals.
 
• It is carried out by specialized cells that proliferate and make large numbers of cells.
 
• Examples include **Hydra** and **Planaria**. While regeneration is a method of producing new individuals, it is fundamentally a process of repair and renewal.
 
 
 
• **Budding**:
 
 
• In organisms like **Yeast** (a unicellular fungus) and **Hydra**, a small outgrowth or 'bud' forms due to repeated cell division at one specific site.
 
• These buds develop into tiny individuals and, when fully mature, detach from the parent body to become independent.
 
 
 
• **Rejuvenation**:
 
 
• In a biological context, this refers to the reversal of the aging process or the restoration of vigor, but it is **not** a recognized method of reproduction in the biological classification of life cycles.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Genetic Stability**: Because fission involves **mitosis** or **amitosis**, it ensures that the **DNA** sequence remains consistent across generations, which is advantageous in stable environments.
 
• **Reproduction Speed**: Under favorable conditions, bacteria like **Escherichia coli** can undergo binary fission every **20 minutes**, leading to exponential population growth.
 
• **Cell Cycle**: In unicellular organisms, the **cell cycle** and the **reproductive cycle** are effectively the same thing, as the division of one cell results in a new organism.
 
• **Environmental Adaptation**: While fission is rapid, the lack of **genetic variation** (unlike sexual reproduction) means the entire population is equally susceptible to environmental changes or **antibiotics**.
</ul
